title.narrative: Strengthening capacities in Serbia to comply with the Enhanced Transparency Framework under the Paris Agreement - CBIT 2

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Strengthening capacities in Serbia to comply with the Enhanced Transparency Framework under the Paris Agreement - CBIT 2, by strengthening Serbia's Policy and Regulatory Framework for transparent climate change reporting, utilizing country-specific tools and data to enhance the Climate Change Transparency System, building institutional and individual capacities for transparent climate policy implementation, and improving Monitoring and Evaluation (ME) and Knowledge Management practices.

The Study on the Socio-economic Aspects of Climate Change in the Republic of Serbia[1] confirms the economy and population's vulnerability to climate change, varying based on factors such as income, expenditures, and activity. Despite potential Gross Domestic Product reductions of up to 3.4% by 2030 and 3.9% by 2050 with associated job losses, investing in GHG emission reduction could mitigate these impacts. While job losses are expected in fossil fuel and agriculture sectors, measures to mitigate heat waves could create new jobs, particularly in forestry-related activities. The Study highlights the need for retraining and an adapted education system to prepare for new practices and sectors with increased employment opportunities. As per the Study findings, investments in reducing GHG emissions align with social goals, as it could limit job losses and stimulate new job creation, particularly in small and medium-sized enterprises and forestry-related sectors. Economic development and climate change adaptation are not mutually exclusive but complementary, offering opportunities for Serbian society to transform during the transition process. The socio-economic benefits from implementation of this project and improved climate change MRV in the Republic of Serbia are potentially significant, with impacts on quality of life, employment, and investments, as well as long-term global benefits such as CO2 reduction. Active involvement from diverse stakeholders like policymakers, energy planners, researchers, businesses, and individuals shall support a successful transition to a low-carbon economy. Through Component 2 of the CBIT 2 project, Serbia's enhanced MRV system will streamline data collection and reporting activities, leading to a more efficient use of public funds. Additionally, this component will support NDC tracking and modeling to estimate the socioeconomic impacts of climate change, providing decision-makers with essential information to set robust targets. Improved MRV in multiple sectors will help Serbia align its policies and measures with current and future NDCs and understand the co-benefits, including socioeconomic benefits, of climate change actions. The socio-economic benefits of this project further extend to key sectors of the economy, including energy and agriculture. In the energy sector, enhanced MRV will enable better planning and enforcement of measures by providing accurate data on energy consumption, emissions, and the effectiveness of energy-saving initiatives. This information will guide policymakers and energy planners in developing strategies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and transition to renewable energy sources, leading to improvements in air quality and public health, as well as job creation in the renewable energy sector. In agriculture, the ETF's improved MRV system will help stakeholders better understand the impacts of climate change on agriculture and support development of Local Adaptation Plans (as per the methodology adopted within CBIT 1 project (GEF ID 10029). By providing reliable data and information, the ETF will support informed decision-making in the agricultural sector, leading to increased productivity, food security, and resilience of rural communities to climate change impacts. Overall, the ETF's enhanced MRV system will contribute to better planning and enforcement of measures by providing stakeholders in the energy and agriculture sectors with accurate data and information. This will support the Republic of Serbia in achieving its climate goals and realizing the socioeconomic benefits of climate change actions.
